newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - March 18.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on March 18:
WASHINGTON - Anthony Lake suddenly withdrew as President Clinton's nominee to be CIA director after concluding there was no end in sight for his confirmation process.
WASHINGTON - House Speaker Newt Gingrich on Monday endorsed the idea of putting off a major tax cut to help achieve a balanced budget deal with President Bill Clinton.
WASHINGTON - Maryland's Democrat-controlled House of Delegates voted overwhelmingly to lower state income taxes by 7 percent.
WASHINGTON - E-mail jokes are spawning bias and harassment suits.

OAKLAND, California - A Texas pilot and businesswoman named Linda Finch set off to circle the globe, following in the footsteps of Amelia Earhart, whose attempt to fly around the world saw her vanish without a trace 60 years ago.
UNITED NATIONS - New Secretary General Kofi Annan announced personnel and financial steps at the United Nations that will trim 1,000 jobs and cut $123 million from the 1998-99 budget.
LONDON - British Prime Minister John Major set May 1 as the date for general elections, kicking off a formal campaign.
